subject: Productization rights and training exclusion — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Allison Park <allison.park@orbitdata.com>

Cc: OrbitData Legal <legal@orbitdata.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — training & output ownership

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OrbitData is excited to move forward. Our legal team attached a redline of the Order Form and a few MSA tweaks focused on two items we need clarity on before procurement can sign:

- Output ownership: We need explicit language that OrbitData retains ownership of all Outputs generated from our uploaded content and prompts.
- Training & feedback license: We cannot agree to language that allows Redwood to use our Outputs or customer content to retrain models that are commercialized or offered to other customers. We can consider an opt-in addendum for model retraining if we separately negotiate commercial terms.

Please see attached: OrbitData_OrderForm_REDLINES.pdf (redline). Our proposed change is narrow — block use of Outputs for model re-training or productization; allow aggregated telemetry/metrics for service reliability only.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and provide a redline back by end of week? If helpful, we can do a short call Monday.

Best,
Allison Park
Director, Vendor Procurement
OrbitData

Allison — thanks for the clear redline. Appreciate OrbitData's specificity; that makes triage easier.

Quick summary of our posture and next steps:
- Output ownership: Redwood's standard Order Form already states customers own Outputs. We'll confirm that clause remains explicit and mirror your suggested language to avoid ambiguity around derivative rights.
- Training & feedback license: Our baseline is that anonymized/aggregated telemetry and service-level feedback may be used to improve the Redwood service (e.g., perf, bug fixes), but we do not, by default, train commercially-distributed models on customer-provided Outputs. That said, customers can opt into a separate training consent addendum with commercial terms.

I've attached a short internal note with proposed language and open questions (RDW_response_notes.docx). Looping in Marcus and Laura to craft a legally-approved counter-redline — Laura, can you please propose wording that both protects Redwood's ability to operate and aligns with OrbitData's ask? Rishi, please flag any product/ops implications (telemetry retention, de-identification).

Happy to do a 30-minute call Monday; Marcus can propose times. We aim to get a clean counter by EOW.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Order Form redlines — training & output ownership

Team — reviewed OrbitData's redline. Below are legal's recommended positions and a proposed counter-clause we can push back with. Key considerations: risk of customer churn if too restrictive vs. operational need to use anonymized signals to maintain service.

Proposed principles:
1) Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Clear statement in Order Form and defined: 'Outputs' = content returned by the Service from Customer inputs.
2) Prohibit use of Customer Outputs and Customer Content for training externally-distributed base models or derivative commercial models absent express, documented opt-in.
3) Permit Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified Outputs and telemetry for internal service improvement (bug fixes, performance tuning, security), subject to standard privacy safeguards and retention limits.
4) Include an opt-in addendum path: if the customer elects to provide training rights, we will negotiate separate compensation and data governance terms.

Draft counter-clause (for Order Form / MSA):
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to the Outputs. Except as authorized by Customer in a separate written agreement, Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or improve models that Redwood commercially distributes or licenses to third parties. Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and metadata derived from Customer's use of the Service solely to operate, secure and improve the Service, provided such data cannot reasonably be re-associated with Customer or individual end-users."

Action items:
- Marcus: propose the commercial framing to OrbitData (we can offer opt-in addendum + fee).
- Rishi: confirm engineering feasibility of the 'de-identified telemetry' constraint and implications for our monitoring/quality flows.
- Tessa: set up a quick call with Allison & OrbitData legal to confirm language.

Attachment: legal_clause_suggestions.txt (includes clause variants and fallback language). Recommend we keep turnaround tight — propose counter out Mon EOD.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: legal_clause_suggestions.txt [text])

Allison — thanks and appreciate the clear ask. Quick commercial note from our side:

- We can accept the proposed prohibition on using Outputs for training/commercial model productization without an opt-in and separate commercial terms.
- To preserve our ability to operate and improve the service we need to retain the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and error traces. We will commit to retention limits (e.g., 12 months) and to not re-associate telemetry to customer data.
- If OrbitData is open to a limited opt-in for retraining, we can offer a separate 'Training Consent Addendum' with defined SLOs, security terms, and a commercial fee.

I attached a short MAP with milestones (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) — propose a 30-minute sync this week to finalize. Would Mon 16:30 or Tue 09:00 PT work?

Thanks — I will prepare the redline that mirrors Laura's draft and include the opt-in addendum language as a separate attachment for OrbitData to review.

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx [spreadsheet])
